target_statement: For every finite nonabelian simple group L and every conjugacy class D of involutions in L, if Gamma is the complete product-order-coloured graph on D and p is the second-smallest distinct prime divisor of |L|, then Aut(Gamma)=Aut_2(Gamma) intersect Aut_p(Gamma).

source_clauses.text: In the notation of Problem 21.52, Gamma is the complete graph on one involution conjugacy class D of a finite nonabelian simple group, with edge colour determined exactly by product order.

For every positive integer t, Aut_t(Gamma) is the set of permutations tau of D that send every edge whose endpoints have product order t to another edge whose endpoints have product order t; if no such edge exists, then Aut_t(Gamma)=S_D vacuously.
Aut(Gamma) is the intersection of Aut_t(Gamma) over all product-order colours t.
Is Aut(Gamma)=Aut_2(Gamma) intersect Aut_p(Gamma), where 2 and p are the two smallest distinct prime divisors of the simple group's order?

constraints.statement: The assertion quantifies over every pair (L,D) satisfying all remaining admissibility rows; the source's G in the question is the group L inherited from Problem 21.52.
L is a finite nonabelian simple group.
D is one conjugacy class in L and every element of D has order exactly 2.
Gamma is the complete simple graph on D, and the colour of an unordered edge {a,b} is determined exactly by the element order |ab| in L.

For every positive integer t (in particular t=2, t=p, and every occurring product-order value), Aut_t(Gamma) consists exactly of the permutations tau of D satisfying |a^tau b^tau|=t whenever a and b are distinct elements of D with |ab|=t. If no edge has product order t, then Aut_t(Gamma)=S_D vacuously.
The primes 2 and p are the two smallest distinct prime divisors of |L|; equivalently p is the smallest prime divisor of |L| greater than 2.
Aut(Gamma) is the group of permutations preserving every product-order colour, equivalently the intersection of Aut_t(Gamma) over all colours t that occur.

excluded_scopes: Problem 21.52's separate assertion that every full colour automorphism is induced by an automorphism of L
A union of multiple involution conjugacy classes
Replacing p by an arbitrary prime divisor rather than the second-smallest distinct prime divisor of |L|
Equality for a bounded list of pairs (L,D) presented as the universal conclusion

success_criteria.proof: Prove the stated two-colour equality for every finite nonabelian simple L and every involution class D.
success_criteria.counterexample: Give a reconstructible finite nonabelian simple L, one involution class D, and a permutation in Aut_2(Gamma) intersect Aut_p(Gamma) that fails to preserve some occurring product-order colour.
partial_progress: A complete independently reproducible determination for a precisely stated infinite family of pairs (L,D).

A complete finite determination for a nontrivial pair (L,D) for which Aut(Gamma)=Aut_2(Gamma) intersect Aut_p(Gamma), together with a reproducible structural explanation. Any finite determination proving strict inequality is a counterexample, not partial progress.
success_criteria.certificate: For a universal proof: a line-by-line proof covering every finite nonabelian simple L and every involution class D, including cases in which a 2- or p-edge set is empty. For a counterexample: a reconstructible finite nonabelian simple L; a verified single conjugacy class D of involutions; the complete product-order matrix on unordered distinct pairs; verification that p is the second-smallest distinct prime divisor of |L|; an explicit tau in S_D; exhaustive checks that tau preserves every edge of product order 2 and p (vacuously if the relevant edge set is empty); and one explicit edge whose product order tau changes. Exact full permutation groups may be supplied but are not required when those membership and separation checks are exhaustive.

truth_likelihood.rationale: Three independently reconstructed nontrivial pairs, including two rank-one groups, satisfy the equality. This modestly favors a structural proof while leaving ample room for a counterexample outside those pairs; the estimate is for scheduling only.

priority.rationale: A finite separating permutation is a compact exact certificate, while equality for structured families can be reconstructed through graph incidence.
